case.pattern_description: The pattern involves structuring multiple online purchases within a short timeframe, with individual amounts kept just under a $500 authorization threshold to evade automated controls. It affects card-not-present channels and was identified through Sentinel sweep anomaly detection analyzing rapid burst transactions within a 21-minute window.

evidence.claim: A sequence of 4 card transactions occurring between 2016-11-25 21:00:00 and 2016-11-25 21:21:00 comprises a single episode totaling $1,935.29 across transaction IDs 3487284, 3487318, 3487340, and 3487348.
Four online purchases executed within a 21-minute span for amounts of $488.31, $489.91, $479.33, and $477.74 demonstrate deliberate structuring under the $500 threshold.
The closed-case classifier evaluated flagged transaction 3487348 at a score of 0.16, aligning with the card's baseline history while the bank risk score registered 0.15.

Device profile MacOS | Mac OS X 10_8_5 | chrome 49.0 | 1280x800 was shared by 2 other cards within the preceding 30 days, with historical associations linked to cases CC-0248, CC-1858, CC-3531, and CC-3811.

Nearest historical matches in case memory consist of CASE-SEN-011, CASE-SEN-008, and CASE-SEN-013, all categorized as undocumented fraud.
Fraud Policy R1 governs verification requirements before blocking on weak signals.
Fraud Policy R3 addresses customer confirmation scenarios resulting in case closure.

Regulatory guidance and typologies include card-not-present fraud, card testing, account takeover, and FATF cyber-enabled fraud red flags.

case.summary: Case SEN-004 was initiated by a Sentinel sweep following a card-not-present structuring pattern on card C03633-K1, belonging to customer C03633. The graph analysis established a fraud probability of 0.90 based on four online purchases executed within 21 minutes, totaling $1,935.29, with amounts kept just under the $500 threshold. Because the fraud probability reached 0.90 and exposure exceeded $1,000, recommended actions include blocking the card, creating a case, and filing a regulatory report under §3a and §6. Prior cases on this customer include CASE-SEN-005.
